summary: Literature opening batch: Spanish international-poll report, distinct French editorial and reader selections, Chinese curricula, Portuguese review and German canon criticism. Genre and methodology differences preserved.
next: Reconsult relevant earlier literary sources individually, then expand regional criticism, independent blogs and reader discussions.

sources.title: La mejor novela de la historia
sources.note: Reports an international writers’ poll favouring Don Quixote; also identifies Proust, Rulfo and García Márquez.
sources.limits: Secondary report of one 2002 poll; mirrors are not independent votes.

sources.title: Pedro Páramo: o romance que colocou a América Latina no mapa da literatura mundial
sources.note: Interprets fractured chronology and uncertain living/dead voices through Faulkner, familial authority and García Márquez; useful formal comparison beyond a list appearance.
sources.limits: Sweeping historical claims are the critic’s interpretation; Portuguese translation details do not verify English editions.

sources.title: Wozu noch Klassiker lesen?
sources.note: Albath connects Lost Illusions with media criticism and Middlemarch with social mechanisms; Baldwin’s delayed German resonance illustrates how local reception changes canon visibility.
sources.location: Timeless subjects, language and canon paragraphs
sources.limits: Illustrative argument favouring classics; current relevance does not by itself establish overall merit.
